text: The wave 3 harness runs in SIT against the owners published contracts with the section 12.8 fakes in place from Day 1, seeds only through the owners published operations, keys every run to the business date the ACE batch record in v_ace_batch_status carries, drives the reconciliation step through the rwb-source-data job operation for JOB-04, asserts REC-04, REC-05 and REC-06 through the rwb-source-data contract, the rwb-payment proceeds read and the rwb-writeoff read, asserts the decision record through the rwb-decision contract, and writes one evidence report per story and business date naming each contract version and whether each hop was a stub or the owner.
why: No source specifies the data product code for the three ACE views, the reconciliation_result read operation and its result codes, the job identifier for JOB-04, the rule package behind REC-04 and REC-06, the rwb-writeoff read operation, the harness environment, the seeding set or the evidence format, so the harness is configured this way for wave 3 and the configuration is agreed at the entry check rather than invented in code.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03, DP-05 and DP-19, R7.2 and R9; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 17, 41, 42, 43 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13, 14 and 15; Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-RDF-007, REQ-RDF-008, REQ-CHO-009, REQ-S7-005 and REQ-DRI-001; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-39 and R-UNI-40; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-PAY-11; legacy RWB-E4-050 sections 1 to 19; Ownership Map entries reconciliation_result, proceeds, write_off, decision_log_entry, rule_row, JOB-04, EV-08, EV-24, EV-25 and EV-26
confirm: Integration lead, QA lead and data product owner at the wave 3 entry check
impact: The harness can run on the fakes from Day 1, and only the real reconciliation step, its result read path and the evidence sign-off wait for the owning stories.

text: reconciliation_result belongs to P1 rwb-source-data as the Ownership Map records it, not to the P8 module the legacy key sat in, so the harness reads the outcome row through the rwb-source-data contract and never as a table, computes no reconciliation of its own, drives the owner JOB-04 step through the owner job operation, and asserts the outcome the owner wrote by rec_code and the business date the ACE batch record carried.
why: The legacy key places the reconciliation and its outcome row in the P8 module while the Ownership Map places reconciliation_result, the reconciliation and JOB-04 with P1 rwb-source-data on Architecture v5 slides 41 and 44, which is higher in the R-PREC order than the story master, so the owner wins and the harness may only read through the owner contract.
read: Template and Rules v1 R3 (R-PREC source precedence) and R5.5 DP-01 and DP-05; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 41 and 44; legacy RWB-E4-050 sections 2 and 12; Ownership Map entries reconciliation_result (owner P1), proceeds (owner P8) and write_off (owner S7); Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-RDF-007 and REQ-RDF-008
confirm: P1 and P8 owners with the integration lead at the wave 3 entry check
impact: The harness asserts the owner outcome and changes nothing itself; the P8 story keeps the proceeds and the match, and P1 keeps the reconciliation, the break list and the outcome row.

text: The approved write-off that REC-06 matches the posting against is read through the rwb-writeoff published contract only, generated as one stub from that contract with its version pinned, and the operation and field names are left as contract placeholders until the rwb-writeoff contract names them, so the harness asserts REC-06 on the write-off key, the amount and the approval the contract returns and invents no operation.
why: No source read in this WP names the operation that reads the approved write-off on the case or the fields that carry its key, amount, posting date and approval, and the harness may not read the rwb_writeoff schema, so the read is pinned to the published contract and the gap row carries the missing names.

text: The wave 3 journey harness runs in SIT against the owning services published contracts with the section 12.8 stub set in place from Day 1, seeds the case only through the owners published operations and never through a schema write, holds one fixed business date and one seeded state per run, and reports every hop with the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the real owner. The product code behind each data product read is a run configuration value, not a business value.
why: No source specifies the harness environment, the seeded identifiers, the data product codes or the wave 3 harness pack, so the harness is configured this way for wave 3 and the configuration is agreed at the entry check rather than invented in code.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.7 rule 6 and R7.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41, 42, 43, 44 and 46; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 17 to 21; legacy RWB-E4-001, RWB-E4-002, RWB-E4-045, RWB-E4-046, RWB-E4-047, RWB-E4-050, RWB-E5-002 and RWB-E5-009; Business Requirements Program v4 sections 5.1 to 5.11.
confirm: Integration lead and QA lead at the wave 3 entry check
impact: The harness can run on the stubs from Day 1, and only the real-owner reruns and the evidence sign-off wait for the owning stories.

text: The business date under test for the wave 3 journey is fixed at 2026-12-14, the ACE batch date the legacy reconciliation key RWB-E4-050 names in its example, and every clock, timer and freshness stamp the journey asserts is read from its owner for that date rather than computed by the harness.
why: No source names a business date for a wave 3 end-to-end journey, and a fixed, source-copied date keeps the run deterministic and the repeated run comparable assertion by assertion.
read: legacy RWB-E4-050 AC1 (v_ace_payment holds three payments for account A-0001 at the ACE batch date 2026-12-14 and v_ace_write_off holds one posting for it); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 (JOB-04 Reconciliation starts on the ACE data ready signal); Template and Rules v1 R7.3.
confirm: QA lead at the wave 3 entry check, with the ACE batch the environment holds for that date
impact: The journey is reproducible for one date, and a date other than the legacy example is a configuration change and not a rewrite of the harness.

text: The harness publishes one evidence report per story and business date, keyed by criterion and holding one trace, the contract version of every hop, whether each hop was a stub or the owner, and the pass or fail of every criterion, and the wave gate passes the release only when every wave 3 harness result recorded for that business date is green, failing the release and naming the harness and the hop when one is red.
why: No source gives an evidence format, a retention period or a gate threshold, and an all-green gate with a keyed per-run report is the least the wave entry check can be held to under Architecture v5 slide 46.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 46 (contract tests per API, event and activity, Temporal replay tests and a daily journey smoke workflow); Template and Rules v1 R7.2 section 16 and R9; legacy RWB-E4-050 and RWB-E5-002 for the criterion shape of the wave 3 keys.
confirm: QA lead and the wave entry check, which may add a threshold beyond all green and a retention period
impact: The gate is usable on Day 1 and can be tightened at the entry check without changing any criterion.

text: Three operations the journey needs are named by no source read, so the harness reads their results through operations that are published: the proof of delivery through the P6 notice read with the case status and the case timers, the guarantee claim through the answer of the S3 create operation and its event, and the JOB-04 reconciliation outcome as records of the rwb-source-data data product. No path is invented for any of them, and each read names the operation and its owner in the evidence report.
why: The ownership map gives P6 GET /notices/{noticeId} with the proof of delivery on the answer and no delivery-confirmation path, gives S3 POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims and PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId} and no claim read path, and gives rwb-source-data no reconciliation read path, so the alternative to this reading is inventing an operation, which the template forbids.
read: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (GET /notices/{noticeId} P6; POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims and PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId} S3; reconciliation_result P1; no reconciliation read path); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17, 19 and 44; legacy RWB-E5-002 and RWB-E4-050.
confirm: The owners of P6, S3 and P1 at the wave 3 entry check, which may publish a delivery-confirmation, a claim read or a reconciliation read instead
impact: The journey runs on published operations only, and a new owner operation changes one hop of the harness and not its criteria.

text: The write-off side of REC-06 and the partner side of the instruction are exercised against the published contracts of S7 rwb-writeoff and S9 rwb-partner with their stubs, because both are wave 4 services, and each stub pass is reported as a stub pass and never as a wave 3 service result; the run is repeated for each when the real owner lands.
why: Architecture v5 slide 41 places rwb-writeoff and rwb-partner in wave 4 while the reconciliation and the instruction are wave 3 behaviour of RWB-E4-050 and RWB-E5-009, so the journey must assert them without waiting for a wave 4 build, and must not present a stub as the owner.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (service catalogue wave column: S7 rwb-writeoff wave 4, S9 rwb-partner wave 4); slide 43 (InstructionIssued produced by rwb-partner); legacy RWB-E4-050 and RWB-E5-009.
confirm: QA lead at the wave 3 entry check, and again when S7 and S9 land in wave 4
impact: The two hops are proven on the contracts from Day 1, and the gate treats them as stub passes until the owners are live.

text: The legacy delivery step is read as three owner facts: the delivery fact on the notice in rwb-comms, the evaluation of R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 and the legal action in rwb-litigation, and the case route move and the notice-period timer in rwb-case; the harness proves the chain across the three, seeds only through published operations, and computes no date, duration, state or rule outcome of its own.
why: No source describes the delivered chain as one operation after the split, and a harness that derived a state or a date would hide exactly the cross-service defect the chain exists to catch.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14, 17, 19, 41 and 42; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (notice, template and merge_field own P6; legal_action and hearing own S4; recovery_case, timer and task own P3); R-LIT-07 and R-LIT-08; DP-01; DP-05

confirm: Solution architect at the wave 3 entry check, with the P3, P6 and S4 owners
impact: The harness owns no schema and no business value; it reports a state it cannot observe as a failed run and not as an assumed pass.

text: The hand-off from the notice to the litigation evaluation is called on the contract the two sibling slices name as RWB-S4-E5002-CON, and the notice write the harness drives is POST /notices/{noticeId}/proof-of-delivery on the rwb-comms base; both names are taken from the sibling slices design until a source names them, and the harness builds against the contract and its fake from Day 1.
why: The TSD P6 appendix ends at API-P6-011 and the TSD S4 appendix ends at API-S4-005, and neither records a proof of delivery, while the legacy step cannot exist without one write and one hand-off.

confirm: The RWB-S4-E5002-CON contract review and the RWB-P6-E5002-APP design review

text: The mapping of a LOV-DELIVERY value onto the notice state is versioned reference data of the business, read at its version in force, and the harness asserts the notice state the owner returns against the delivery status it sent rather than applying a mapping of its own; a PENDING status is treated as a proof that is not back yet and moves nothing.
why: LOV-DELIVERY carries DELIVERED, REFUSED, UNDELIVERABLE and PENDING and the SCR-18 list carries generated, approved, sent, delivered and unserved, but no source states which value produces which state or what PENDING means for the notice.
read: LDM v8 DF-LEG-022 (LOV-DELIVERY); TSD P6 T3.2 list; legacy RWB-E5-002 screen block (SCR-18 Notice approval: generated, approved, sent, delivered, unserved); R-LIT-07 and R-LIT-08
confirm: The reference-data owner in rwb-case and the rwb-comms owner at the P6 design review
impact: A changed mapping is a reference-row change and not a harness change; a run that finds no mapping row for a status fails instead of guessing.

text: The notice-period clock is a durable timer inside CaseWorkflow in rwb-case, its timer row is the projection read through GET /cases/{caseId}/timers, and the notice-period duration is a versioned reference row; the harness asserts started_at against the delivered date and expires_at against the end the owner publishes, and never computes an end date itself.
why: The legacy key names a timer table and a notice period, the ownership map puts the timer and the timer clock with rwb-case, and the duration is a business value no source read states.
read: Legacy RWB-E5-002 data block (timer, DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036); TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 (timer); Architecture v5 slide 44 (durable timers, JOB-05 retired); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json timer ruling; CTL-15; R-LIT-07
